skill.name: backend-dev-guidelines
skill.description: Backend development guidelines for Node.js, Express, TypeScript, Prisma, Sentry, Zod, and layered service architecture.
skill.summary: Guides agents through consistent backend service design, validation, configuration, monitoring, and testing patterns.
skill.author: Dimon94

security_audit.summary: Static scanner hits are false positives from Markdown guidance, TypeScript imports, placeholders, and code examples rather than executable skill behavior. No prompt-injection text was found. A medium semantic issue remains because the Sentry template may over-collect request and user telemetry if copied without stronger scrubbing.

remediation.issue: Sentry examples collect broad request and user context.
remediation.suggestion: Set requestDataIntegration to the minimum needed fields and scrub request bodies, query values, IP addresses, custom sensitive headers, and user email before sending events.

remediation.issue: Configuration examples include placeholder secrets and development defaults.
remediation.suggestion: Mark all sample secrets as non-production placeholders and validate required secrets at startup with no weak fallback in production.

remediation.issue: Examples use fixed config files that contain secrets.
remediation.suggestion: Keep config.ini, .env, certificate, and key files ignored by version control and prefer managed secret stores for production deployments.

content.value_statement: Backend services often drift into mixed patterns and hard-to-test code. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured guidance for Express, Prisma, validation, monitoring, and tests.
actual_capabilities: Explains layered backend architecture using routes, controllers, services, repositories, and middleware.
Provides TypeScript and Express patterns for controllers, route delegation, and error handling.
Documents Prisma repository patterns, transactions, query optimization, and testing mocks.
Shows Zod validation patterns for route input, DTOs, error responses, and schema composition.
Guides Sentry setup, async error handling, performance spans, and cron job monitoring.
Includes full examples for user management features, service tests, and route refactoring.
limitations: It is guidance content, not an executable backend generator.
Examples assume Node.js, Express, TypeScript, Prisma, Jest, Zod, and Sentry.
Project-specific paths and service names must be adapted before use.
Security-sensitive telemetry and secret handling still need human review.

use_cases.title: Create a New API Feature
use_cases.description: Use the route, controller, service, validation, and repository patterns to add a feature with consistent structure.

use_cases.title: Refactor Legacy Routes
use_cases.description: Move business logic out of large Express route files into controllers and services with clearer responsibilities.

use_cases.title: Standardize Service Quality
use_cases.description: Apply shared rules for configuration, Sentry monitoring, Prisma access, async errors, and backend test coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Backend Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Using the backend development guidelines, outline the route, controller, service, validation, repository, and test files for a new feature.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Express Route
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Express route against the backend guidelines. Identify business logic, validation gaps, error handling gaps, and a refactoring plan.

prompt_templates.title: Design Prisma Access
prompt_templates.prompt: Design the service and repository layer for this Prisma workflow. Include transaction boundaries, query optimization, errors, and unit test strategy.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Observability and Config
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this backend service against the guidelines for unifiedConfig, Sentry instrumentation, async error handling, middleware order, and sensitive data exposure.

output_examples.input: A user route contains validation, database writes, and response formatting in one handler.
output: A refactoring plan separates routing, controller logic, service rules, and repository access.
The controller handles request parsing, Zod validation, success responses, and error delegation.
The service owns business rules and calls a repository for Prisma operations.

output_examples.input: A service needs consistent error tracking and async handling.
output: The response recommends try-catch boundaries, specific custom errors, and Sentry capture points.
It notes where sensitive context should be reduced before sending telemetry.
It suggests tests for success, validation failure, repository failure, and authorization failure.

output_examples.input: A team wants one pattern for configuration across microservices.
output_examples.output: The guidance recommends centralized typed configuration, startup validation, production environment variables, and avoiding scattered direct environment access.

best_practices: Use the guidelines as a review checklist before generating or changing backend code.
Adapt service names, paths, and domain models to the target repository before applying examples.
Review telemetry, secrets, and authentication behavior before merging generated backend changes.
anti_patterns: Do not copy examples without checking security-sensitive defaults and project-specific middleware.
Do not keep business logic, validation, and database writes inside route handlers.
Do not send full request bodies, secrets, or sensitive user details to monitoring tools.

faq.question: Which projects fit this skill best?
faq.answer: It fits Node.js and TypeScript backend services that use Express, Prisma, Zod, Jest, and Sentry.

faq.question: Can it generate a complete service?
faq.answer: It provides structure and examples, but generated code still needs repository-specific integration and review.

faq.question: Does it replace security review?
faq.answer: No. It includes security-aware patterns, but secrets, telemetry, and authorization need human review.

faq.question: Why does it mention direct environment access?
faq.answer: The guidance uses those examples to discourage scattered process.env reads and prefer typed configuration.

faq.question: Can teams use it for refactoring?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes patterns for moving route logic into controllers, services, and repositories.

faq.question: What tools are supported?
faq.answer: The report marks it compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
